newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HBG says German units to break even in 97.
newsitem.headline: HBG says German units to break even in 97.

text.p: Dutch builder Hollandsche Beton Groep NV said on Tuesday it did not see the German construction market recovering in 1997, but that both its loss-making unit Raulf Bau and newly-acquired Wayss&Freytag were seen breaking even.

"In years past there was enormous growth in German construction output but currently it is down with all the resultant consequences for margins," HBG chairman Nic de Ronde Bresser told a news conference.
Due to the continued stagnation of the German economy there was little prospect of improved volumes and margins over the next two years, he said.
Nevertheless HBG expected the contribution to group results of Raulf Bau GmbH and Wayss&Freytag to be neutral, he said.
Wayss&Freytag, in which HBG acquired a 74 percent stake late last December, earlier reported a full-year net loss of 90 million marks in 1996.
"Wayss&Freytag will show a significant improvement and will have a neutral effect on HBG's result (in 1997)," finance director Dick Sinninghe Damste said.
"They (Weyss&Freitag) have indicated they will reach a neutral result," he added.
Raulf Bau closed 1996 with an unspecified loss, mainly due to losses incurred on a major project in Berlin, De Ronde Bresser said.
However, these losses had now been capped and further losses looked to be be avoided this year. "Raulf Bau is seen breaking even in 1997," Sinninghe Damste said.
In 1996 HBG derived some 11 percent of total turnover in Germany. As a result of the Wayss&Freytag acquisition this is seen growing sharply to 35 percent in 1997, it said.

HBG said in a statement that while neither Wayss&Freytag nor its British acquisition Higgs&Hill were seen contributing to profits in the first few years, the new positioning of HBG would bear fruit in the longer term.
